Shamash.fact: Shamash (Akkadian: šamaš), also called Utu (written 𒀭𒌓; Sumerian: dutu, literally "Sun"), was the ancient Mesopotamian sun god.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: Additionally, he could serve as the god of divination, typically alongside the weather god _____
Shamash.fact: Additionally, he could serve as the god of divination, typically alongside the weather god Adad.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: While he was universally regarded as one of the primary gods, he was particularly venerated in _____ and Larsa
Shamash.fact: While he was universally regarded as one of the primary gods, he was particularly venerated in Sippar and Larsa.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: The moon god Nanna (Sin) and his wife _____ were regarded as his parents, while his twin sister was Inanna (Ishtar)
Shamash.fact: The moon god Nanna (Sin) and his wife Ningal were regarded as his parents, while his twin sister was Inanna (Ishtar).

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: Occasionally other goddesses, such as Manzat and _____, could be regarded as his sisters too
Shamash.fact: Occasionally other goddesses, such as Manzat and Pinikir, could be regarded as his sisters too.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: The dawn goddess Aya (_____) was his wife, and multiple texts describe their daily reunions taking place on a mountain where the sun was believed to set
Shamash.fact: The dawn goddess Aya (Sherida) was his wife, and multiple texts describe their daily reunions taking place on a mountain where the sun was believed to set.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: Among their children were _____, the personification of truth, dream deities such as Mamu, as well as the god Ishum
Shamash.fact: Among their children were Kittum, the personification of truth, dream deities such as Mamu, as well as the god Ishum.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: The connection between him and the _____ solar god Shimige is particularly well attested, and the latter could be associated with Aya as well
Shamash.fact: The connection between him and the Hurrian solar god Shimige is particularly well attested, and the latter could be associated with Aya as well.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: While no myths focusing on Utu are known, he often appears as an ally of other figures in both _____ and Akkadian compositions
Shamash.fact: While no myths focusing on Utu are known, he often appears as an ally of other figures in both Sumerian and Akkadian compositions.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: According to narratives about _____'s death, he helped protect him when the galla demons tried to drag him to the underworld
Shamash.fact: According to narratives about Dumuzi's death, he helped protect him when the galla demons tried to drag him to the underworld.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: In various versions of the Epic of _____ and in earlier Gilgamesh myths, he helps this hero defeat the monstrous Humbaba
Shamash.fact: In various versions of the Epic of Gilgamesh and in earlier Gilgamesh myths, he helps this hero defeat the monstrous Humbaba.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: In the myth _____ and An, he helps his sister acquire the temple Eanna
Shamash.fact: In the myth Inanna and An, he helps his sister acquire the temple Eanna.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: In How Grain Came to Sumer, he is invoked to advise Ninazu and _____
Shamash.fact: In How Grain Came to Sumer, he is invoked to advise Ninazu and Ninmada.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: A further relatively commonly attested name is _____, whose origin is uncertain
Shamash.fact: A further relatively commonly attested name is Amna, whose origin is uncertain. The most common writing of the sun god's name was the logogram dUTU, which could be read as Utu, Shamash, or, as attested in the god list An = Anum, as Amna.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: The ancient _____ form of the name was most likely Śameš, though many variant syllabic spellings are attested
Shamash.fact: The ancient Aramaic form of the name was most likely Śameš, though many variant syllabic spellings are attested.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: Manfred Krebernik notes that a well known example of a female deity in what he deems the "cuneiform cultural sphere" is _____
Shamash.fact: Manfred Krebernik notes that a well known example of a female deity in what he deems the "cuneiform cultural sphere" is Shapash.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: At the same time, both the _____ and the Arameans viewed the solar deity as male, like Sumerians and Akkadians
Shamash.fact: At the same time, both the Amorites and the Arameans viewed the solar deity as male, like Sumerians and Akkadians.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: In the _____ god list from Fara, he is the sixth among the deities listed, after Anu, Enlil, Inanna, Enki and Nanna
Shamash.fact: In the Early Dynastic god list from Fara, he is the sixth among the deities listed, after Anu, Enlil, Inanna, Enki and Nanna.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: In later god lists, for example in An = Anum, he and his circle appears between Nanna (Sin) and _____ (Adad)
Shamash.fact: In later god lists, for example in An = Anum, he and his circle appears between Nanna (Sin) and Ishkur (Adad). The Old Babylonian Nippur god list instead places him between Ishkur and Ninurta.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: The Old Babylonian Nippur god list instead places him between Ishkur and _____
Shamash.fact: The Old Babylonian Nippur god list instead places him between Ishkur and Ninurta.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: Common epithets characterize Utu as a "youth" (_____ šul, Akkadian eṭlu) and "hero" (Sumerian ursaĝ, Akkadian qarrādu)
Shamash.fact: Common epithets characterize Utu as a "youth" (Sumerian šul, Akkadian eṭlu) and "hero" (Sumerian ursaĝ, Akkadian qarrādu).

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: Manfred Krebernik argues that in early sources, his chariot was drawn by lions, but this has been questioned by _____
Shamash.fact: Manfred Krebernik argues that in early sources, his chariot was drawn by lions, but this has been questioned by Marco Bonechi.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: He could be assisted in this role by his father Nanna, his sister _____, and various minor judge deities
Shamash.fact: He could be assisted in this role by his father Nanna, his sister Inanna, and various minor judge deities.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: A hymn to Utu states that _____ cannot give judgment without his presence
Shamash.fact: At least in the third millennium BCE, Ishtaran was regarded as a divine judge equal in rank to Utu, and a fragment of a myth from Ebla mentions a divine tribunal in which they both partake alongside Idlurugu (dÍD), a river god also known for his association with justice and judgment who represented ordeal by water. A hymn to Utu states that Idlurugu cannot give judgment without his presence.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: As an extension of his role as a divine judge, Utu could be associated with the underworld, though this connection is not attested before the _____ period
Shamash.fact: As an extension of his role as a divine judge, Utu could be associated with the underworld, though this connection is not attested before the Old Babylonian period.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: In this capacity he could be associated with the deified legendary king _____, commonly portrayed in a similar role
Shamash.fact: In this capacity he could be associated with the deified legendary king Gilgamesh, commonly portrayed in a similar role.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: The connection between the sun god and the weather god is well attested in _____ sources and goes back to the Old Babylonian period
Shamash.fact: The connection between the sun god and the weather god is well attested in Mesopotamian sources and goes back to the Old Babylonian period.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: Subsequently, he taught it to the people of Sippar, Nippur and _____
Shamash.fact: The connection between the sun god and the weather god is well attested in Mesopotamian sources and goes back to the Old Babylonian period. Subsequently, he taught it to the people of Sippar, Nippur and Babylon.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: Due to distinct attributes, he is considered one of the few _____ deities who can be identified in art with certainty
Shamash.fact: Due to distinct attributes, he is considered one of the few Mesopotamian deities who can be identified in art with certainty.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: Depictions of him are known from many sites, for example _____, Tell al-Rimah, Sippar, Ur and Susa
Shamash.fact: Depictions of him are known from many sites, for example Eshnunna, Tell al-Rimah, Sippar, Ur and Susa.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: Christopher Woods points out that both in _____ and Akkadian, judgments had to be "cut" (kud/parāsum), and therefore considers the association with judgment to be most likely
Shamash.fact: Christopher Woods points out that both in Sumerian and Akkadian, judgments had to be "cut" (kud/parāsum), and therefore considers the association with judgment to be most likely.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: On seals from the _____ period, he could be depicted climbing over two mountains, which has been interpreted as a representation of sunrise
Shamash.fact: On seals from the Sargonic period, he could be depicted climbing over two mountains, which has been interpreted as a representation of sunrise.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: The attendant deity is sometimes interpreted as _____
Shamash.fact: The attendant deity is sometimes interpreted as Bunene.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: In some cases _____ is shown watching the battle or partaking in it on Utu's side
Shamash.fact: In some cases Inanna is shown watching the battle or partaking in it on Utu's side.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: One well known example of such an image is a stele of _____ of Babylon, inscribed with his legal code
Shamash.fact: One well known example of such an image is a stele of Hammurabi of Babylon, inscribed with his legal code.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: It is commonly discussed in scholarship, and has been described as "one of the masterpieces of ancient Near Eastern art." It was discovered by Hormuzd Rassam in December _____ during his excavations i
Shamash.fact: It is commonly discussed in scholarship, and has been described as "one of the masterpieces of ancient Near Eastern art." It was discovered by Hormuzd Rassam in December 1880 during his excavations in Abu Habbah in modern Iraq.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: Its discovery subsequently made it possible to identify this site with _____
Shamash.fact: Its discovery subsequently made it possible to identify this site with Sippar.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: It dates to the Neo-_____ period, but its style has been described as "archaizing," and most likely was inspired by motifs found in presentation scenes from the Ur III period
Shamash.fact: It dates to the Neo-Babylonian period, but its style has been described as "archaizing," and most likely was inspired by motifs found in presentation scenes from the Ur III period.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: While other anthropomorphic depictions of the sun god are known from _____ from the same period, in Babylonia he came to be usually portrayed in the form of a symbol instead
Shamash.fact: While other anthropomorphic depictions of the sun god are known from Assyria from the same period, in Babylonia he came to be usually portrayed in the form of a symbol instead.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: It is attested as early as in the _____ period, and continued to be represented in art through the rest of history of ancient Mesopotamia
Shamash.fact: It is attested as early as in the Sargonic period, and continued to be represented in art through the rest of history of ancient Mesopotamia.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: Additionally the symbol of a winged sun came to be associated with the sun god in _____ in the first millennium BCE
Shamash.fact: Additionally the symbol of a winged sun came to be associated with the sun god in Assyria in the first millennium BCE.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: It only arrived in _____ during the reign of Nabonidus
Shamash.fact: It only arrived in Babylonia during the reign of Nabonidus.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: They are already attested as father and son in the _____ god list from Fara
Shamash.fact: They are already attested as father and son in the Early Dynastic god list from Fara.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: Ningal was regarded as Utu's mother, and _____ as his sister
Shamash.fact: Ningal was regarded as Utu's mother, and Inanna as his sister. Due to her identification with Ishtar (Inanna) the Hurrian and Elamite goddess Pinikir is called a twin sister of Shamash and daughter of Sin (Nanna) and Ningal in a text written in Akkadian but found in a corpus of Hurro-Hittite rituals.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: Hymn to the Queen of _____ refers to them as twins
Shamash.fact: Hymn to the Queen of Nippur refers to them as twins.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: The sun god's wife was invariably the goddess of dawn and light, usually known under the name Aya, though the forms Ninkar, Sudaĝ, _____ and Sudgan are also well attested
Shamash.fact: The sun god's wife was invariably the goddess of dawn and light, usually known under the name Aya, though the forms Ninkar, Sudaĝ, Sherida and Sudgan are also well attested.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: Aya was believed to intercede with her husband on behalf of worshipers, which is a function also well attested for other divine spouses, such as _____ and Shala
Shamash.fact: Aya was believed to intercede with her husband on behalf of worshipers, which is a function also well attested for other divine spouses, such as Ninmug and Shala.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: It has also been pointed out that in the case of Inanna, her sukkal _____ fulfilled a similar role
Shamash.fact: It has also been pointed out that in the case of Inanna, her sukkal Ninshubur fulfilled a similar role.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: In legal texts from _____, the sun god and his wife commonly appear as divine witnesses
Shamash.fact: Utu/Shamash and Aya are the single most common divine couple in cylinder seal inscriptions from Sippar, with only the number of dedications to Ishkur and Shala being comparably high. In legal texts from Sippar, the sun god and his wife commonly appear as divine witnesses.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: The only other divine couple attested in this role in this city are Mamu and _____
Shamash.fact: The only other divine couple attested in this role in this city are Mamu and Bunene.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: In myths both about himself and about _____, the legendary king Enmerkar was referred to as a son of Utu
Shamash.fact: In myths both about himself and about Lugalbanda, the legendary king Enmerkar was called a son of Utu. Unlike other legendary kings of Uruk, namely Lugalbanda and Gilgamesh, Enmerkar was not deified, despite the existence of a tradition attributing divine ancestry to him.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: Unlike other legendary kings of Uruk, namely _____ and Gilgamesh, Enmerkar was not deified, despite the existence of a tradition attributing divine ancestry to him
Shamash.fact: In myths both about himself and about Lugalbanda, the legendary king Enmerkar was called a son of Utu. Unlike other legendary kings of Uruk, namely Lugalbanda and Gilgamesh, Enmerkar was not deified, despite the existence of a tradition attributing divine ancestry to him.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: However, in the _____ is instead his grandfather, and his father is a human ruler, Meškiağašer
Shamash.fact: However, in the Sumerian King List Utu is instead his grandfather, and his father is a human ruler, Meškiağašer.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: In various sources, Utu seems to serve as a special protector to several of _____'s other kings
Shamash.fact: Unlike other legendary kings of Uruk, namely Lugalbanda and Gilgamesh, Enmerkar was not deified, despite the existence of a tradition attributing divine ancestry to him. In various sources, Utu seems to serve as a special protector to several of Uruk's other kings.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: Bunene, also known under the name _____, was considered his chariot driver
Shamash.fact: Bunene, also known under the name Papnunna, was considered his chariot driver.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: He is attested in multiple theophoric names, chiefly from _____
Shamash.fact: He is attested in multiple theophoric names, chiefly from Sippar.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: Some researchers, including _____ and Manfred Krebernik, consider the reading of the second element of his name to be uncertain due to variable orthography, and transcribe it as Nin-PIRIG
Shamash.fact: Some researchers, including Antoine Cavigneaux and Manfred Krebernik, consider the reading of the second element of his name to be uncertain due to variable orthography, and transcribe it as Nin-PIRIG.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: The pair _____ and Nigsisa, whose names mean "law" and "order," respectively, are identified as the "vizier of the left" and "vizier of the right" in the god list An = Anum
Shamash.fact: The pair Nigzida and Nigsisa, whose names mean "law" and "order," respectively, are identified as the "vizier of the left" and "vizier of the right" in the god list An = Anum. Nigzida could be equated with Niggina, another goddess regarded as the sun god's sukkal, though the latter deity's role varies between that of a servant and oldest daughter in known copies of the god list An = Anum.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: Her Akkadian counterpart was _____, whose name has the same meaning, "truth." In An = Anum Kittum is instead male and a brother of Niggina
Shamash.fact: Her Akkadian counterpart was Kittum, whose name has the same meaning, "truth." In An = Anum Kittum is instead male and a brother of Niggina.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: She had a sukkal of her own, _____-damiq
Shamash.fact: She had a sukkal of her own, Iqbi-damiq.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: None of Utu's sukkals known from other sources are present in documents from the archive of the _____ dynasty
Shamash.fact: None of Utu's sukkals known from other sources are present in documents from the archive of the First Sealand dynasty.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: Lugal-namtarra is otherwise sparsely attested and might be analogous to _____
Shamash.fact: Odette Boivin proposes that in local tradition, this role was instead fulfilled by the deities Lugal-namtarra and dSUKKAL, who frequently appear alongside the sun god, and that the former functioned as his sukkal during his nightly journey through the underworld, while the latter fulfilled the same role during the day. Lugal-namtarra is otherwise sparsely attested and might be analogous to Namtar.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: One well known example of such a deity is _____, who could also be associated with Inshushinak and Lagamal
Shamash.fact: It has been suggested that it is a symbolic representation of a conflict between day and night, or that the deities confronted by Utu and his allies are rebellious mountain gods. Wilfred G. Lambert suggested that in some cases figures from battle scenes with rays emanating from their shoulders might be representations of Enmesharra rather than the sun god, as in a tradition known from a late myth, Enmesharra's Defeat, he was their original owner.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: In the _____ of Gilgamesh, a scorpion man and a scorpion woman guard the mountain of sunrise
Shamash.fact: In the Standard Babylonian Epic of Gilgamesh, a scorpion man and a scorpion woman guard the mountain of sunrise.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: He proposes that it was a result of the well attested association between the sun god and _____, whose servant Nirah usually was
Shamash.fact: He proposes that it was a result of the well attested association between the sun god and Ishtaran, whose servant Nirah usually was.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: Joan Goodnick Westenholz proposed that Ninkar in _____ texts should be interpreted as Ninkarrak rather than the phonetically similar but more obscure Mesopotamian Ninkar
Shamash.fact: Alfonso Archi instead concludes that the deity was primarily female based on lexical evidence, but points out that the Eblaites were definitely aware of the male eastern sun god, and seemingly adopted him into their pantheon as a secondary hypostasis. Joan Goodnick Westenholz proposed that Ninkar in Eblaite texts should be interpreted as Ninkarrak rather than the phonetically similar but more obscure Mesopotamian Ninkar.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: Occasional shortening of _____'s name to "Ninkar" is known from Mesopotamian sources as well
Shamash.fact: Joan Goodnick Westenholz proposed that Ninkar in Eblaite texts should be interpreted as Ninkarrak rather than the phonetically similar but more obscure Mesopotamian Ninkar. Occasional shortening of Ninkarrak's name to "Ninkar" is known from Mesopotamian sources as well.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: This theory is also accepted by Archi, who notes it makes the widespread worship of _____ easier to explain
Shamash.fact: Joan Goodnick Westenholz proposed that Ninkar in Eblaite texts should be interpreted as Ninkarrak rather than the phonetically similar but more obscure Mesopotamian Ninkar. Occasional shortening of Ninkarrak's name to "Ninkar" is known from Mesopotamian sources as well.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: The Hurrian sun god, _____, is already represented by the logogram dUTU in an inscription of Atalshen, an early king of Urkesh
Shamash.fact: The Hurrian sun god, Shimige, is already represented by the logogram dUTU in an inscription of Atalshen, an early king of Urkesh.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: He is directly equated with Utu in the trilingual Sumero-Hurro-_____ version of the Weidner god list from Ugarit
Shamash.fact: He is directly equated with Utu in the trilingual Sumero-Hurro-Ugaritic version of the Weidner god list from Ugarit.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: It has been argued that his character was influenced at least in part by his _____ counterpart
Shamash.fact: It has been argued that his character was influenced at least in part by his Mesopotamian counterpart.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: Gary Beckman goes as far as suggesting that at least in _____ texts, he "cannot (yet?) be distinguished sufficiently" from the latter
Shamash.fact: Gary Beckman goes as far as suggesting that at least in Hittite texts, he "cannot (yet?) be distinguished sufficiently" from the latter.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: Due to this association, Aya was regarded as his spouse in _____ tradition, as attested in sources from Hattusa and Ugarit
Shamash.fact: Due to this association, Aya was regarded as his spouse in Hurrian tradition, as attested in sources from Hattusa and Ugarit. Shimige is additionally equated with Lugalbanda in it, most likely because the Hurrian pantheon was smaller than that enumerated in Mesopotamian lists, creating the need to have a single Hurrian deity correspond to multiple Mesopotamian ones.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: In the trilingual god list, _____ (transcribed as dwu-u-un-ni-nu-wa-an) appears in association with Shimige
Shamash.fact: In the trilingual god list, Bunene (transcribed as dwu-u-un-ni-nu-wa-an) appears in association with Shimige.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: The same list also attests the equivalence between Utu, _____ and the Ugaritic sun goddess Šapšu
Shamash.fact: In the trilingual god list, Bunene (transcribed as dwu-u-un-ni-nu-wa-an) appears in association with Shimige. Shimige is additionally equated with Lugalbanda in it, most likely because the Hurrian pantheon was smaller than that enumerated in Mesopotamian lists, creating the need to have a single Hurrian deity correspond to multiple Mesopotamian ones.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: Apparently to avoid the implications that _____ had a wife, the scribes interpreted the name of Aya, present in the Sumerian original, as an unconventional writing of Ea
Shamash.fact: Apparently to avoid the implications that Shapash had a wife, the scribes interpreted the name of Aya, present in the Sumerian original, as an unconventional writing of Ea.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: Instead of the _____ spelling of Aya, the name Eyan corresponds to him in the Hurrian column and Ugaritic one lists the local craftsman god Kothar-wa-Khasis
Shamash.fact: Shimige is additionally equated with Lugalbanda in it, most likely because the Hurrian pantheon was smaller than that enumerated in Mesopotamian lists, creating the need to have a single Hurrian deity correspond to multiple Mesopotamian ones. Instead of the Hurrian spelling of Aya, the name Eyan corresponds to him in the Hurrian column and Ugaritic one lists the local craftsman god Kothar-wa-Khasis.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: The logogram dUTU is well attested in _____ texts
Shamash.fact: The logogram dUTU is well attested in Hittite texts. Gary Beckman notes that the Hittite conception of solar deities does not show any Indo-European influence, and instead was largely similar to that known from Mesopotamia.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: Gary Beckman notes that the _____ conception of solar deities does not show any Indo-European influence, and instead was largely similar to that known from Mesopotamia
Shamash.fact: The logogram dUTU is well attested in Hittite texts. Gary Beckman notes that the Hittite conception of solar deities does not show any Indo-European influence, and instead was largely similar to that known from Mesopotamia.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: The logogram dUTU also designated the sun deity or deities in Emar in the late _____
Shamash.fact: The logogram dUTU also designated the sun deity or deities in Emar in the late Bronze Age.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: According to _____, the Mesopotamian, West Semitic, Hurrian and Hittite sun deities might all be potentially represented by it in texts from this city
Shamash.fact: Gary Beckman notes that the Hittite conception of solar deities does not show any Indo-European influence, and instead was largely similar to that known from Mesopotamia. According to Gary Beckman, the Mesopotamian, West Semitic, Hurrian and Hittite sun deities might all be potentially represented by it in texts from this city.

Shamash.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Shamash.question: It is possible that in legal texts, when dUTU occurs next to _____ deities Inshushinak, Ruhurater or Simut, the latter option is correct
Shamash.fact: It is possible that in legal texts, when dUTU occurs next to Elamite deities Inshushinak, Ruhurater or Simut, the latter option is correct.
